correctness.rationale: The maximally mixed input and Schur–Weyl decomposition give spin-\(j\) lowest-weight eigenvalue \((2j+1)/2^n\), multiplicity \(g_{n,k}\), and excitation \(k\). Passive rank sorting is exact. Stirling plus a matching binomial-tail lower window establish a tail of order \(2^n n^{-2c^2+o(1)}\). The Casimir identity \(\mathbb E[J_n(J_n+1)]=3n/4\) forces excess large-spin mass to vanish. Uniform Hoeffding tails and uniform integrability yield the asymptotic normalized work coefficient \(1/2\). Independent dark-space matrix checks for \(n\le7\), and exact passive sorting checks for \(n<40\), returned VERIFY_OK. Finite checks corroborate rather than prove the limit.

value.rationale: The nontrivial logarithmic enhancement over ordinary \(\sqrt n\) collective-spin fluctuations and the sharp \(1/2\) leading coefficient specify work capacity in a natural known dissipative battery at a singular thermal endpoint. The quantity is global ergotropy, not an arbitrary slice; finite plots and positive-work statements cannot determine this asymptotic. The result isolates an entropy/quantile mechanism for comparing thermal and imperfectly collective models without claiming such extensions.
